title: Competitive and non-competitive inhibitors
caption: A competitive inhibitor fights the substrate for the active site, so more substrate overcomes it: the curve shifts right (Km up) but reaches the same Vmax. A non-competitive inhibitor binds elsewhere and puts some enzyme out of action, so substrate cannot overcome it: Vmax falls.
alt: Three rate curves against substrate concentration: no inhibitor, a competitive inhibitor that shifts the curve right to the same maximum, and a non-competitive inhibitor that lowers the maximum.
description: Competitive inhibitor: Km rises to 6 but the curve still approaches Vmax 100.
Non-competitive inhibitor: Vmax falls to 60; Km stays at 2.
Competitive inhibition is overcome by raising the substrate concentration; non-competitive inhibition is not.

checks.name: competitive: half of Vmax (50) is reached at [S] = 6, so Km has risen from 2 to 6
competitive: at very high [S] the rate reaches the same Vmax, 100
competitive: at the same [S] the rate is lower than with no inhibitor
non-competitive: half of its own Vmax (30) is reached at [S] = 2, so Km is unchanged
non-competitive: Vmax falls to 60, and more substrate cannot restore it
